prompt: Add up what the paying parties are asked for in March 2027 on the Ekene ledger: forecast 12000000.000000, January's 400000 over-call arriving under a two-month lag, credits carried, threshold 500000.000000.
options: 12000000.000000, the whole forecast, the credit waiting for the year-end reconciliation
11200000.000000, March's own actual, since a call is trued up to the month's spend
The forecast with the credit added on top
explanation: March's month row prints calls of 11600000.000000 on a forecast of 12000000.000000: January's over-call reaches March two months later and reduces each paying party's call by its own January difference. 11200000.000000 is March's actual, known only after the call. A credit lowers a call; it never raises it.

prompt: On the Ekene ledger (lag 2 months, rule "carry", threshold 500000.000000), EKO over-calls by 200000.000000 in January and under-calls by -250000.000000 in February. What balance with the operator does EKO hold at the end of February 2027?
options: 200000.000000, since February's under-call is not counted until the call it adjusts
-250000.000000, February's difference alone, as January's credit was used up in February
0.000000, the January credit and the February under-call cancelling out
explanation: EKO's February row prints a balance of -50000.000000: both differences are still waiting for the calls their lag names, and the balance with the operator counts the differences not yet adjusted. January's credit is used in March, so it is still held at the end of February.

prompt: October 2027 on the Ekene ledger (lag 2 months, rule "carry", threshold 500000.000000) meets two things at once: August's under-call and the credit carried from September. What does EKO's October row show?
options: An adjustment of 100000.000000, the carried credit alone, since an under-call waits for the month after a carried credit is spent
An adjustment of -52000.000000, August's under-call alone, the carried credit waiting a month
A call of 4000000.000000, the forecast share, with both items netted at the close
An adjustment of 48000.000000 and a call of 3952000.000000 on a forecast share of 4000000.000000
explanation: The engine applies both in October: "2027-10: the under-call of 104000 in 2027-08 (forecast 3000000, actual 3104000) is added to this cash call, 2 months later" and "2027-10: a credit of 200000 held from 2027-09 is applied to this cash call". EKO's row prints an adjustment of 48000.000000 and a call of 3952000.000000.

prompt: EKO's forecast share for December 2027 is 2500000.000000, and October's under-call of 400000 reaches that call under the Ekene terms (lag 2, carry, threshold 500000.000000). What is EKO asked for?
options: The forecast share less the under-call, as if it were a credit
2700000.000000 on a forecast share of 2500000.000000, its adjustment being -200000.000000
2500000.000000, as an under-call is billed in arrears in the next month
The whole 400000 under-call added to EKO's call alone as operator
explanation: An under-call adds to the call it reaches: EKO's December row prints an adjustment of -200000.000000, its half of October's 400000, and a call of 2700000.000000, the engine's reason naming October's forecast of 8000000 and actual of 8400000. Treating the under-call as a credit moves the call the wrong way, and arrears billing is only for spend made in a month with no call.

prompt: Three parties (A 50, B 30, C 20 percent) run cc-zero-call-month: a one-month lag, credits carried, no threshold. January over-calls by 200 and February is forecast at 0.000000. What happens in February and March?
options: February is called at 0.000000 with 200.000000 carried; March is called 200.000000 on a forecast of 400.000000
February makes no call, its forecast being 0; January's credit waits and March is called 400.000000
February is called -200.000000, the credit refunded; March is called 400.000000
February and March are each called 0.000000
explanation: With no threshold, February is called: "2027-02: a forecast of 0: the cash call is the adjustment alone", and under "carry" the credit waits ("the call is 0 and the rest of the credit is carried to the next cash call"). March applies it: "2027-03: a credit of 200 held from 2027-02 is applied to this cash call". A negative call of -200.000000 is the "refund" rule's answer.

prompt: A ledger's final month, December 2027, is forecast at just 100.000000 against a threshold of 500 (cc-last-month-uncalled, two-month lag, credits carried) and spends 120.000000. How is December treated?
options: It calls the 100.000000 anyway, since the last month of a ledger is always called to close the year
It refuses the ledger, as its last month cannot be billed in arrears inside the months given
It makes no call, and its reason says the actual is billed in arrears in the next month
It adds December's 120.000000 to November's call
explanation: The forecast of 100 is below the stated threshold, so December is not called: "2027-12: no cash call: the forecast 100 is below the stated threshold 500; the actual is billed in arrears in the next month". A month's own call is never re-opened, and the last month gets no special rule.

prompt: A cash call ledger lists 2027-01 and then 2027-03 as its first two months. What does the engine return?
options: A ledger that treats February as a month with a zero forecast and calls only the adjustment in it
A ledger of two months, the gap ignored, with January's difference adjusting the March call
A ledger in which the missing month is billed in arrears in March
A refusal naming months[1].month, which must be 2027-02, the months being consecutive
explanation: The engine refuses the gap, in its own words: months[1].month must be 2027-02, the month after 2027-01 (the months are consecutive); got "2027-03". It invents no missing month and skips nothing, because the lag counts calendar months.

prompt: The golden input carry-partial-stated states parties A 60, B 20 and N 20 percent, a compound uplift of 12.5 percent and carry recovery from 50 percent of N's share. 2029 opens at 12.500000 with 100.000000 available. What is recovered in 2029?
options: 12.500000, the opening balance, since a carried party pays no uplift on an uplift
14.062500, the balance with its uplift of 1.562500
100.000000, the whole amount available
12.500000, with 1.562500 written off
explanation: The uplift is charged on the opening balance, 12.5 percent of 12.500000 being 1.562500, and the balance of 14.062500 is less than the 100.000000 available: "2029: the balance 14.06 is recovered with 14.06 of the 100 available; the carried party receives 185.94 of its share 200". Compounding charges uplift on an uplift carried forward, and nothing is written off without a cap.

prompt: On the Ekene carry (compound 8.000000 percent a year on the opening balance, carry recovery from 50.000000 percent of NOC's share, basis "contract"), 2030 is the first year NOC has entitlement. What closes 2030?
options: What is left once the whole share of 19200000.000000 is taken against the balance
32088960.000000, the opening balance, since the carry recovery starts in the year after the first entitlement
What is left with the uplift charged only after the year's carry recovery is taken off
explanation: The engine's reason reads "2030: 9600000 recovered of 34656076.8 due; 25056076.8 carried to 2031". The stated carry recovery share is 50 percent of the share of 19200000.000000, so 9600000.000000 is available, and the uplift of 2567116.800000 is charged on the opening 32088960.000000 before the year-end carry recovery.

prompt: Across 2027 to 2036, how much uplift does the 8.000000 percent compound Ekene carry (half of NOC's share, basis "contract") earn in all, and how much do the carriers get back on their 28400000.000000?
options: An uplift of 14200000.000000 and 42600000.000000 recovered
An uplift of 9529407.979520 and 25000000.000000 recovered
An uplift of 10067760.617882 and 38467760.617882 recovered
An uplift of 0.000000 and 28400000.000000 recovered, the Act barring any uplift on the Ekene carry
explanation: The totals print carried cost 28400000.000000, uplift 10067760.617882, recovered 38467760.617882 and nothing written off, recovered in 2033. 14200000.000000 and 42600000.000000 are the 150 percent multiple's totals; 9529407.979520 and 25000000.000000 are the capped carry's. The Act's bar on uplift applies under basis "pia-s85-4", which this carry does not state.

prompt: Which carrier gains from an uplift? At 0.100000 to 2027, EKO's value is 95024921.509253 when the Ekene carry compounds at 8.000000 percent from half of NOC's share under a contract. What is it when the carry follows s.85(4), with no uplift, from the whole share?
options: 92668197.518975, lower, as EKO recovers no uplift
95024921.509253, unchanged, since EKO's NPV depends only on its own costs and entitlement
96139876.399404, higher, since EKO is repaid sooner and so gains in value
54584252.437515, the carried party's figure
explanation: The canonical npv returns EKO 92668197.518975 on the Act's carry against 95024921.509253 on the compound carry: the carrier gives up the uplift. 96139876.399404 is EKO's NPV under the 150 percent multiple. 54584252.437515 is NOC's NPV on the Act's carry.

prompt: A learner builds a carryRecovery call on the Ekene carry and leaves out the basis. What does the engine return?
options: A carry recovery under the contract basis, the Act's basis applying only when stated
A carry recovery under the Act, since NOC is the state participant
A carry recovery with no basis line in its report
Refused, the basis being a required term the engine picks for no caller
explanation: The basis is a required term: the engine refuses a call without it and chooses neither basis for the caller. Only the stated basis "pia-s85-4" brings in the Act's bar on uplift; a party's name brings in nothing.

prompt: In the first year of NOC's entitlement after its back-in to 40 percent under the Act (half its new share available), how much of the refund of 98000000.000000 is paid back, and what is left?
options: 38400000.000000 recovered, the whole new share, as the Act takes the refund from future production
19200000.000000 recovered of NOC's share of 38400000.000000, and 78800000.000000 carried to 2031
9600000.000000 recovered, half of NOC's old 20 percent share
Nothing recovered until 2031, a year after participation
explanation: The engine's reason reads "2030: 19200000 recovered of 98000000 due; 78800000 carried to 2031"; NOC's new share of 38400000.000000 makes 19200000.000000 available at the stated 50 percent, and NOC receives the other 19200000.000000. The refund recovery reads the new share after the back-in.

prompt: On backin-pia-at-60 NOC backs in from 20 to 60 percent under basis "pia-s85-4". What does EKO hold after it, and what refund does it receive?
options: 0.000000, EKO ceding all 40 points as operator, and a refund of 196000000.000000
30.000000, as in the back-in to 40, and a refund of 49000000.000000
20.000000, and no refund, since at the ceiling the Act refunds nothing
20.000000, keeping 40 / 80 of its 40, and a refund of 98000000.000000
explanation: The engine's reason reads "NOC backs in from 20% to 60%: the others keep 40 / 80 of their interests; refund 40% x refundable costs 490000000 = 196000000 (156000000 excluded)"; its table prints EKO after 20.000000 and a refund received of 98000000.000000, in proportion to the 20.000000 points EKO gives up.

prompt: On backin-ekene-contract-upfront (basis "contract", refundable kinds stated to include exploration), what reason does the engine give for the signature bonus of 10000000.000000?
options: It is not refundable, being not a stated refundable kind
It is not refundable under PIA s.85(4)(c), the Act's list applying to every back-in
It is refundable, a bonus being a proven cost of the licence
It is refundable at 20 percent, NOC's change of participating interest
explanation: Under a contract basis the reason reads "signature bonus: 10000000 (bonus) is not refundable (not a stated refundable kind)". The same line under the Act reads the s.85(4)(c) citation. The basis decides which list applies.

prompt: Under basis "contract", a learner forgets to list which cost kinds may be refunded. What comes back?
options: A back-in using the Act's development and production list
A back-in in which every cost line is refundable
A refusal: under a contract the refundable kinds must be stated, with no default
A back-in in which no line is refundable, the refund being 0.000000

The Act's list is used only under "pia-s85-4", and a contract's list is never guessed.

prompt: Paid in one sum on entry (refundForm "upfront", basis "contract"), a refund is typed together with a list of future years. What comes back?
options: An upfront refund, with the years serving to discount it
A refusal naming years, which must be left out when the refund is paid upfront
A refund recovered from the stated years, the upfront form set aside
A refusal naming refundForm, since an upfront refund is barred on every basis
explanation: The engine refuses the extra term: years must be left out when refundForm is "upfront". An upfront refund has no refund recovery ledger. The bar on an upfront refund is the Act's and applies under "pia-s85-4"; the contract-basis case backin-ekene-contract-upfront returns a refund of 125200000.000000.

prompt: Suppose PB never cures its Ekene default and the call is read at 2027-07-01, with simple default interest at 8.250000 percent on 360 days and no grace. What does the engine charge?
options: 55569.791577 on 4 whole months, the method switching to monthly once a month has passed
20625.000000, the default interest stopping at the cure date the fixture states
56718.750000, the default interest received by EKO when it covers two defaulters
explanation: The engine's reason reads "interest 2000000 x 8.25% x 122 days / 360 = 55916.67 (from 2027-03-01 to asOf 2027-07-01, the default still open, the last date excluded)". 55569.791577 is the monthly-compound case; the method is a stated term. An open default runs to asOf.

prompt: On default-monthly-compound-uncured PB's 2000000.000000 is still unpaid four months after its due date, at 8.25 percent compounded monthly on 360 days with a 72-hour grace. What is charged?
options: 55569.791577, on 4 whole months and 0 days
0.000000, the 72-hour grace suspending default interest while a default is open
56718.750000, compounding the four months and the 72 hours of grace on top
explanation: The reason prints "interest 2000000 x ((1 + 8.25% / 12)^4 x (1 + 8.25% x 0 days / 360) - 1), 4 whole months and 0 days = 55569.79". 55916.666667 is the simple figure on the same days. The 72 hours are long past, and under its stated grace the engine then counts from the due date itself.

prompt: On default-monthly-compound-whole-months PB (2000000.000000 unpaid, 8.250000 percent, monthly-compound, 360-day basis, grace 0 hours) cures on 2027-05-01, due 2027-03-01. What does the engine count?
options: 61 days simple, the month count being used only for defaults still open
1 whole month and 30 remaining days
27594.531250: two whole months, no days left over
2 whole months and 1 remaining day, the cure date counted in
explanation: A cure on a month anniversary gives whole months only: "interest 2000000 x ((1 + 8.25% / 12)^2 x (1 + 8.25% x 0 days / 360) - 1), 2 whole months and 0 days = 27594.53". The cure date is excluded, and months keep the day of the month.

prompt: On default-monthly-compound-month-end party C owes 200000.000000 from 2027-01-31, open at asOf 2027-04-15, at 12 percent, monthly-compound, 365-day basis, grace 0 hours. How does the engine count the time?
options: 74 days simple on a 365-day year
2 whole months and then 15 days, giving 5026.126027
2 whole months ending 2027-03-28, February's last day kept as the day of the month, then the rest as days
3 whole months, the part-month rounded up
explanation: The reason prints "interest 200000 x ((1 + 12% / 12)^2 x (1 + 12% x 15 days / 365) - 1), 2 whole months and 15 days = 5026.13"; the field is 5026.126027. A month from a month end keeps the day of the month, the last day when the month is shorter.

prompt: PB's Ekene default earns 20625.000000 of default interest (8.250000 percent, simple, 360-day basis, grace 0 hours, cured 2027-04-15). How does the engine share it, as it states its cover?

EKO alone, as the operator that administers the joint account
EKO, PA and NOC by participating interest
EKO 12692.307692 and PA 7932.692308, in proportion to their cover

prompt: Party C's default on default-working-days-holiday states suspension after 5 working-days from 2027-12-22, with stated holidays. When does the engine put the trigger?
options: After 2028-01-03, working days being Monday to Friday less the stated holidays
After five calendar days, the weekend and the holidays counted like any other day
After the fifth weekday, the stated holidays ignored since the engine keeps no calendar of them
After 2028-01-05, the asOf date, since a suspension waits for the date the call is read at

prompt: PB's Ekene default states forfeiture after 3 months from 2027-03-10, a trigger date of 2027-06-10. The default is still open at asOf 2027-06-10 on one golden input and at asOf 2027-06-11 on another. What does the engine report?

Not triggered on either, forfeiture needing a fourth month
Not triggered at 2027-06-10; triggered at 2027-06-11
Triggered at 2027-06-10 and reported with the compensation computed

The compensation on an assignment is reported only; the engine computes none.

prompt: A contract's default interest states a day basis of 366. What does the engine return?

A refusal: interest.dayBasis must be 365 or 360; got 366
Default interest on a 365-day year, the nearest basis the engine accepts
Default interest on a 360-day year, the Norwegian agreement's basis

Royalty 27375000.000000, cost recovered 131400000.000000 and profit oil 60225000.000000

prompt: Add up the government's take over the ten years of the Ekene PSC variant, whose terms are a 12.5 percent royalty, cost oil capped at 60 percent of gross, a 60 percent contractor share, 30 percent tax and 142000000.000000 of opening pool. How much is it, and how much of it is tax?

prompt: By 2038 the Ekene variant's pool is gone and opex is 28000000.000000 (a limit of 60 on gross after a 12.5 royalty). What is recovered, and against what limit?

28000000.000000 recovered against a limit of 56563200.000000
49492800.000000 recovered, the limit binding

prompt: A 60.000000 percent limit is tried on both bases for 2030 of the Ekene PSC variant (12.5 royalty, 60 share, 30 tax, 142000000.000000 carried in). How much profit oil is left on each?

Profit oil of 60225000.000000 with the gross limit, 76650000.000000 with the after-royalty one

191625000.000000 on both, the revenue after royalty

prompt: A learner types costRecoveryLimitPct in place of the engine's term for the limit. What does the engine return?

A PSC run with no limit, the unknown key dropped

Refused by name as a key the engine does not read, with its accepted keys listed

prompt: PIA 2021 s.311(2)(a)(iii) sets a cost oil limit of not more than 60 percent for a renegotiated PSC. What does the engine do with that figure?

It caps every stated costOilLimitPct at 60, the Act's ceiling for a renegotiated contract
It applies 60 percent of gross as the limit whenever a PSC call leaves the cost oil limit unstated
It refuses any limit above 60 under basis "pia-s85-4", as it refuses a back-in above 60

The limit is a required input.

prompt: Divide the one-barrel profit oil of IMF FARI TNM/16/01 (February 2016) Figure 5 as the engine does: the contractor holds 40 percent of it, cost oil is capped at half of what royalty leaves, tax is 30 percent, there is no royalty, costs reach the cap, and the barrel sells for 100. Contractor 20.000000 and government 36.000000
explanation: The engine returns contractor profit oil 20.000000 and government profit oil 30.000000, as the figure prints. 26.000000 and 39.000000 are the World Bank note's split, and 36.000000 is the government's profit oil and tax together.

prompt: In 2008 of the IMF schedule (psc-fari-table-12), Table 13 prints the contractor's profit petroleum as 181. What does the engine return, and how does the course read the gap?

182.000000, a gap the validation record reports as a defect in applyPSC and leaves open for the reader to settle
A share one lower, the engine truncating it

The course bounds the split more widely than the cost lines, since the tables print the government's share to a whole per cent, and every year of the schedule falls inside that wider bound. Nothing is rounded to match a table, and the record finds no defect.

prompt: OpenOil, Oil Contracts: How to read and understand them (version 1, November 2012) prints "This is calculated by: 0.25 x 49 = 11.75 million dollars". How does the course use the book?

It quotes the book's 11.75 as its result
It is a licensed text, taught by concept only
It uses no schedule from it and teaches its state participation example as a printed arithmetic error
explanation: The sources table records OpenOil, version 1, November 2012, Creative Commons: no schedule is used, and its state participation example is taught as a printed arithmetic error. A figure copied from a reference text is checked before it is taught.

prompt: NOC is carried in full on the Ekene joint venture. Reading the 2027 cash call ledger (lag 2, "carry", threshold 500000.000000) and the compound carry together, what happens to NOC's cost share in 2027?
options: NOC is called 0.000000 every month, and its carried cost of 16400000.000000 opens its carry balance
NOC is called 20 percent of each forecast and the carriers repay it at the year end
NOC is called nothing and owes nothing, the carry being a gift of its cost share
NOC's share is billed in arrears in December and the carry covers it
explanation: Every NOC row of the ledger prints a call of 0.000000 on a paying interest of 0.000000, and the carry ledger's 2027 row carries NOC's cost of 16400000.000000 to 2028, to be recovered from NOC's share of entitlement from 2030. A carry is financing to be recovered.

prompt: Both the Ekene carry under the Act (carry-ekene-pia, carry recovery from 100.000000 percent of the share) and the Ekene back-in (backin-ekene-pia, refund from 50.000000 percent of NOC's new share) state basis "pia-s85-4". What do they share, and when does each close?
options: Both carry the Act's uplift; the carry closes in 2033 and the refund in 2031
Neither carries an uplift; both close in 2031
Neither carries an uplift; the carry is recovered in 2031 and the refund in 2034
Both take the whole share; both close in 2034
explanation: Under "pia-s85-4" the carry's uplift must be none (s.85(4)(c)) and the refund is "recovered with no uplift". The carry is recovered in 2031 and the refund in 2034, each on its own balance and stated share.

prompt: Which of these contract terms may a call leave out and still get a result?
options: The reconciliation lag of a cash call ledger
The cash call threshold, noCallBelow
The uplift of a carry recovery
The grace hours of default interest
explanation: cc-ekene-2027-every-month runs with no threshold and returns calls of 69052000.000000. The lag, the uplift and the grace are required terms with no default, each refused by name when missing ("reconciliationLagMonths must be an integer at or above 1; got nothing").

prompt: The engine cites the Act for both a back-in and PSC cost recovery. Which provisions does each call's basis cite?
options: Both cite s.85(4), the carried interest provision
backIn cites s.311(2)(a)(iii); pscCostRecovery cites s.85(4)
Neither cites the Act, both citing the Norwegian agreement
backIn cites PIA s.85(4); pscCostRecovery cites s.85(2)(a) and s.311(2)(a)(iii) with applyPSC
explanation: The engine's basis.source for backIn reads the Petroleum Industry Act 2021 (Act No. 6), Official Gazette No. 142, Vol. 108, 27 August 2021 s.85(4); for pscCostRecovery it adds s.85(2)(a) and s.311(2)(a)(iii) and engines/economics/cashflow.ts applyPSC. Section 85(4) governs the concession agreement of s.85(2)(d).

prompt: The Kenya Model PSC 2015, Participation Agreement, is quoted in the cash call module and the default module. Which of its figures does the engine hold?
options: None: its rate and grace are stated inputs and no refund timing is held; the golden input states the 72 hours
The 72-hour grace of Art. 6.7, which the engine applies whenever a contract states no grace of its own
The margin over LIBOR that Art. 6.7 prints, which the engine adds to every stated default interest rate
The fifteen-day refund of an excess advance
explanation: Every contractual rate, grace and rule is a stated input with no default. The Kenya case states its grace ("rate and grace stated here"), and the model leaves the margin over LIBOR blank. A missing grace is refused by name.

prompt: On the Ekene joint venture, cash calls and the PSC variant split costs between the same four partners. Does each split on paying or on participating interests, and what does NOC bear?
options: Both use paying interests, so NOC pays nothing in either
Both use participating interests, so NOC pays 20 percent in both
Cash calls use paying interests (NOC 0.000000); the PSC splits by participating interest (NOC -56000000.000000 of the 2029 capex)
